material_events.basis: stated in P4 (10-Q MD&A), P6 (8-K earnings release), and P7 (8-K Item 8.01)
material_events.claim: Talen Energy Marketing closed on a capacity monetization agreement to sell rights to approximately $1.5 billion in future PJM capacity cash flows for the 2027/2028 and 2028/2029 PJM Capacity Years, with net proceeds of $1.3 billion used to fund accelerated share repurchases.
quotes: On October 1, 2026, TEM closed on a capacity monetization agreement to sell rights to approximately $1.5 billion in future PJM capacity cash flows for the 2027/2028 and 2028/2029 PJM Capacity Years and the Company used the net proceeds of $1.3 billion to fund accelerated share repurchases.

TEM transferred the rights of future cash flows for certain cleared capacity with volumes of approximately 6.5 GW and 6.0 GW for the 2027/2028 and 2028/2029 delivery years, respectively, and aggregate revenues of approximately $1.5 billion.

material_events.basis: stated in P4 (10-Q MD&A), P6 (8-K earnings release), and P7 (8-K Item 8.01)
material_events.claim: The Board approved upsizing the share repurchase program to an aggregate remaining capacity of $3 billion, and the Company received and retired 3,811,460 shares under a $1.5 billion accelerated share repurchase program equivalent to 80% of the ASR value.
quotes: In September 2026, the Board of Directors approved the upsizing of the Company's existing SRP from $1.5 billion to an aggregate remaining capacity of $3 billion, subject to utilization under the ASR program.

On October 1, 2026, the Company received and retired 3,811,460 shares of TEC common stock repurchased under ASR program with multiple dealers, which is equivalent to 80% of the aggregate $1.5 billion value of the ASR program.

material_events.claim: Talen Energy announced that Terry L. Nutt will become CEO and President effective January 1, 2027, and that current CEO Mark "Mac" A. McFarland will step down as CEO and Board member effective the same date.
quotes: the Company's board of directors (the "Board") has named Terry L. Nutt as the Company's next Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") and President, effective January 1, 2027
Mark "Mac" A. McFarland, the Company's current CEO, has given the Company notice of his intent to step down as CEO and as a member of the Board, effective on the Effective Date.

Total Equity | 1,603 | 1,093

Upon completion of the ASR program at current prices, we will have repurchased approximately 19.5 million shares of TEC common stock for a total of approximately $4.0 billion since the start of 2024, with $1.5 billion remaining under our SRP through year end 2028.

risks.basis: stated in P1 (business description of PJM and FERC delay), P3 (MD&A capacity markets section), and P4 (Q3 2026 MD&A capacity markets section)
risks.claim: PJM has delayed its capacity auctions and the FERC has accepted requests to propose additional changes to the PJM Reliability Pricing Model, creating uncertainty over the timing and structure of future capacity revenue that Talen depends on for the substantial majority of its revenues.
quotes: the FERC has accepted requests by PJM to delay certain PJM BRAs in order to propose additional changes to the PJM Reliability Pricing Model
Recently, PJM has delayed its auctions, which has resulted in less than 3 years between each auction and the start of the relevant PJM Capacity Year.
The substantial majority of our generation capacity is located in, and accordingly the majority of our revenues are derived from, PJM.

risks.basis: stated in P2 (risk factors, nuclear section) and P1 (business description of Susquehanna and AWS PPA)
risks.claim: Susquehanna accounts for a substantial amount of Talen's generation and earnings; an unplanned outage, catastrophic event, or regulatory action affecting the nuclear plant would materially reduce output and revenue, and could impair the company's ability to meet its AWS PPA delivery obligations.
quotes: Because Susquehanna accounts for a substantial amount of our generation and associated earnings, any adverse development in Susquehanna's operations, such as an unplanned outage or catastrophic event, could have a significant impact on our business.

a significant operational disruption at Susquehanna could impair our ability to meet our PJM Capacity Performance requirements and our obligations under long-term power supply contracts, including under the AWS PPA

risks.basis: stated in P2 (risk factors, demand growth section) and P1 (business description, demand growth section)
risks.claim: The improved market outlook for competitive wholesale power generation depends largely on expected future demand from data centers, re-shoring, and electrification; if this demand does not materialize or is sustained, energy and capacity prices could fall, reducing Talen's margins and the value of its generation fleet.
quotes: Expected demand growth from the technology sector, manufacturing, and other uses of electricity, which has driven recent improvements in the outlook for the competitive wholesale power generation market, may not actually occur or be sustained.

Various factors including but not limited to unfavorable macroeconomic conditions, increases in energy efficiency or supply, or advances in technology, could result in lower-than-expected electricity demand and unfavorable market conditions for our business.

risks.basis: stated in P7 (8-K Item 8.01, capacity monetization description) and P4 (Q3 2026 MD&A, recent developments)
risks.claim: Talen sold approximately $1.5 billion of future PJM capacity cash flows for the 2027/2028 and 2028/2029 delivery years to fund share repurchases, permanently reducing future capacity revenue and free cash flow that would otherwise have been available to service debt or support operations.
